INSUFFICIENT_SOLDER.name: Insufficient solder
INSUFFICIENT_SOLDER.description: Solder fillet does not meet minimum wetting / fill requirements per IPC-A-610.

EXCESS_SOLDER.name: Excess solder
EXCESS_SOLDER.description: Solder volume exceeds maximum fillet / pad envelope, may obscure inspection or violate clearances.

SOLDER_BRIDGE.name: Solder bridge / short
SOLDER_BRIDGE.description: Unwanted solder connection between two adjacent conductive features that should be electrically isolated.

COLD_SOLDER.name: Cold / disturbed solder joint
COLD_SOLDER.description: Joint with grainy / dull surface or fractured appearance from insufficient heat or movement during solidification.

SOLDER_BALL.name: Solder ball
SOLDER_BALL.description: Free / loose solder spheres on the assembly that may migrate and cause shorts.

SOLDER_VOID.name: Solder void (BGA / QFN)
SOLDER_VOID.description: Internal cavity within a solder joint exceeding the area-percent limit (typically >25% Class 2, >9% Class 3 thermal pads).

NON_WETTING.name: Non-wetting
NON_WETTING.description: Solder did not wet to a metallic surface; original surface remains visible.

DEWETTING.name: Dewetting
DEWETTING.description: Solder initially wet then receded, leaving irregular mounds and exposed base metal.

EXPOSED_BASE_METAL.name: Exposed base metal
EXPOSED_BASE_METAL.description: Conductor base metal visible where coating / solder is required by design.

FLUX_RESIDUE.name: Flux residue
FLUX_RESIDUE.description: Visible flux residue beyond cleanliness limits; acceptable for no-clean within visual limits.

TOMBSTONING.name: Tombstoning
TOMBSTONING.description: Chip component lifted vertically off one pad, often due to uneven reflow heating.

BILLBOARDING.name: Billboarding
BILLBOARDING.description: Chip component standing on its side rather than seated flat.

MISALIGNMENT.name: Component misalignment / offset
MISALIGNMENT.description: Component offset from pad exceeds the side-overhang or end-overhang limit for the class.

MISSING_COMPONENT.name: Missing component
MISSING_COMPONENT.description: Component absent from designated location per BOM / design.

WRONG_COMPONENT.name: Wrong component
WRONG_COMPONENT.description: Component value / part number does not match BOM.

REVERSED_POLARITY.name: Reversed polarity
REVERSED_POLARITY.description: Polarised component (diode, electrolytic cap, IC) installed in opposite orientation.

LIFTED_LEAD.name: Lifted lead
LIFTED_LEAD.description: Component lead not in contact with pad / solder fillet.

BENT_LEAD.name: Bent / damaged lead
BENT_LEAD.description: Lead deformation beyond formed-lead tolerance, may impair coplanarity.

INSUFFICIENT_HOLE_FILL.name: Insufficient hole fill (THT)
INSUFFICIENT_HOLE_FILL.description: Vertical solder fill in plated through-hole below 75% (Class 2) or 100% (Class 3).

PIN_PROTRUSION_INSUFFICIENT.name: Insufficient pin protrusion
PIN_PROTRUSION_INSUFFICIENT.description: Lead does not protrude sufficiently beyond solder side of board.

CONTAMINATION_PARTICULATE.name: Particulate contamination
CONTAMINATION_PARTICULATE.description: Loose particles, FOD or debris on assembly surface.

MARKING_ILLEGIBLE.name: Illegible marking / label
MARKING_ILLEGIBLE.description: Required marking unreadable due to smear, low contrast or print defect.

BARCODE_UNREADABLE.name: Barcode / 2D-DMC unreadable
BARCODE_UNREADABLE.description: Machine-readable code fails decode at required quality grade (typically ISO/IEC 15415 grade C minimum).

PCB_SCRATCH.name: PCB surface scratch
PCB_SCRATCH.description: Surface scratch on PCB substrate or solder mask not exposing copper.

SOLDERMASK_DAMAGE.name: Solder mask damage
SOLDERMASK_DAMAGE.description: Lifted, missing or cracked solder mask exposing conductor.

LAMINATE_DAMAGE.name: Laminate damage / measling
LAMINATE_DAMAGE.description: Internal separation / white spots in PCB laminate (measling, crazing, blistering).

DAMAGED_INSULATION.name: Damaged wire insulation
DAMAGED_INSULATION.description: Cut, burn or abrasion in wire insulation exposing conductor.

EDGE_BURR.name: Edge burr (machined housing)
EDGE_BURR.description: Sharp burr along machined edge exceeding max allowed height.

CHIP_OUT.name: Chip-out / edge break
CHIP_OUT.description: Material chipped from edge or corner, breaking the design profile.

DENT.name: Dent / deformation
DENT.description: Localised inward deformation beyond cosmetic / functional limit.

COSMETIC_SCRATCH.description: Surface scratch on visible cosmetic area exceeding zone (A/B/C) length / width spec.

introduction.title: System Introduction
introduction.content:
The Continuum system is a comprehensive solution for monitoring, analyzing, and managing automatic inspection machines in manufacturing plants.

The system provides real-time monitoring, inspection data analysis, productivity reports, and product quality management.

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.content:
The system is built with a layered architecture:

• UI Layer: Responsive web and mobile application
• API Layer: RESTful API and tRPC for communication
• Business Layer: Logic and business rules processing
• Data Layer: PostgreSQL with DrizzleORM
• MQTT: Real-time communication with AOI machines

dataFlow.title: Data Flow
dataFlow.content:
Inspection data is collected from AOI machines via MQTT and processed in real-time.

• AOI machines send inspection results via MQTT
• Server receives and stores data in the database
• Dashboard updates automatically via WebSocket
• Alerts are triggered based on defined rules

connectMachine.question: How do I connect an AOI machine to the system?
connectMachine.answer:
To connect an AOI machine, you need to:
1. Configure MQTT broker in Settings > MQTT Configuration
2. Set up topic pattern matching the AOI machine
3. Ensure the AOI machine is configured to send data to the correct broker and topic
4. Check the connection in the MQTT Monitor page

yieldNotUpdating.question: Why is the yield rate not updating?
yieldNotUpdating.answer:
If the yield rate is not updating, check:
1. Is the MQTT connection active (see MQTT Monitor)
2. Is the AOI machine sending data
3. Is the topic subscribed correctly
4. Is the message format correct

lowYieldAlert.question: How do I set up an alert for low yield?
lowYieldAlert.answer:
To set up a low yield alert:
1. Go to Alerts > Alert Rules
2. Click Create New Rule
3. Select metric 'Yield Rate'
4. Set condition 'Less Than' and desired threshold
5. Configure notification method and recipients
6. Save and activate the rule

autoReport.question: How do I set up automatic email reports?
autoReport.answer:
To set up automatic reports:
1. Configure SMTP in Admin > Settings > SMTP Configuration
2. Go to Reports > Scheduled Reports
3. Create a new scheduled report
4. Choose template, content, and frequency
5. Add recipient email list
6. Activate the schedule

fixNtf.question: What is NTF and how do I reduce the NTF rate?
fixNtf.answer:
NTF (No Trouble Found) are products marked as defective by the AOI machine but found to have no actual defects upon re-inspection.

To reduce NTF rate:
1. Optimize inspection parameters on the AOI machine
2. Improve lighting conditions
3. Update golden samples regularly
4. Analyze NTF patterns to adjust algorithms

maxPoints.question: What is the maximum number of inspection points per PCB?
maxPoints.answer: The maximum number of inspection points depends on the AOI machine configuration and inspection program. The Continuum system can handle thousands of inspection points per PCB. For optimal performance, it is recommended to limit to under 5000 inspection points per board.
